# The eve of Badr: seven messages for the WhatsApp pilot (experiment X6)
# Draft. Not reviewed. A teacher reads each one before it is sent.

Day 1
The eve of Badr. Today we stand at Badr. Madinah is 117 km to the north-east, in a straight line.

Day 2
The text says: "on Friday, the morning of the seventeenth of Ramaḍān" (Ibn Hishām, al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya, vol. 1, p. 626). Question for tomorrow: what would the moon have looked like that night?

Day 3
Computed, not reported: on the modern calendar's reckoning (Tuesday 13 March 624) the moon was 96% lit. The date conversion itself is uncertain, so scholars keep the reported date and the converted one apart.

Day 4
A puzzle: the text gives a total of 314 for this list (All Muslims present at Badr, or given a share). 313 in the well-known report, 314 in Ibn Isḥāq's list. Before tomorrow, guess: does the list of names hold more, fewer or exactly 314?

Day 5
Answer: the reading of the list found 321 names. They differ. Scholars keep three things apart: what happened, the text, and our reading of the text.

Day 6
The text gives the weekday: Friday. None of the three computed lunations falls on that weekday under a simple crescent rule: a question for the scholars.

Day 7
The text names 496 people at this event: 314 with the Prophet ﷺ and 131 on the other side.
